subtopics.name: Upper GI disorders and GI bleeding

questions.stem: Use the client's data to fill in the diagram: the problem this client most likely has, 2 actions for the nurse, and 2 parameters to track.

actions.text: Start the octreotide infusion as prescribed
Prepare for urgent endoscopic band ligation
Insert a nasogastric tube to suction
Give a large saline bolus to a normal blood pressure

rationale.correct: Variceal bleeding: octreotide, antibiotics, restrictive transfusion and urgent banding; track hemoglobin and hemodynamics.

perOption.c1: Cirrhosis with large-volume bright red hematemesis and shock.
perOption.c2: Possible, but cirrhosis with portal hypertension makes varices most likely.
perOption.a4: Beta blockers prevent rebleeding later; they worsen acute shock.
perOption.a5: Overfilling raises portal pressure; transfuse to a modest target.
perOption.p1: Guides transfusion, usually to about 7 to 8 g/dL.

options.text: Needs follow-up: adjust insulin in the bag or the dextrose

perOption.b3:a: A short half-life protein that responds to feeding.

questions.stem: On a GI surgical unit, the nurse receives these updates at 0800. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client 1 day after gastric bypass whose heart rate rose from 96 to 128/min, feeling anxious
A client with a new colostomy whose stoma is red and moist and who has not yet passed any stool
A client with cirrhosis on lactulose who reports three soft stools since midnight
A client the day after laparoscopic cholecystectomy who reports right shoulder pain and asks for a heating pad

rationale.correct: New tachycardia after bariatric surgery may be the only early sign of a leak.

perOption.a: Sustained tachycardia after bypass is the earliest sign of an anastomotic leak.
perOption.d: Referred gas pain after laparoscopy is common.

questions.stem: Which tasks can the RN delegate to the unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) for a client receiving continuous enteral tube feeding? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the head of the bed at 30 degrees or higher
Measure and record the volume of feeding given
Report coughing or vomiting during the feeding at once
Check tube placement before restarting the feeding
Give medications through the feeding tube

rationale.correct: UAPs can position, measure, report and give mouth care; placement checks and medications stay with licensed nurses.

perOption.f: Medication administration is not delegated to UAP.

questions.stem: The leak was repaired and the client was discharged. At 4 weeks, the client reports cramping, diarrhea, a racing heart and dizziness 20 minutes after meals. Which teaching should the nurse give? Select all that apply.

options.text: Eat six small meals rich in protein
Wait 30 minutes after meals before drinking fluids
Drink a large glass of juice with each meal
Eat a high-carbohydrate snack before bed

rationale.correct: Early dumping is prevented with small protein meals, avoiding sugars and separating fluids from meals.

perOption.c: Fluids with meals speed food into the bowel.
perOption.e: Can cause late dumping and hypoglycemia.

questions.stem: At 3 months, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I take my vitamin B12, iron and calcium citrate every day."
"I'll use acetaminophen, not ibuprofen, for headaches."
"I'll get my labs checked as scheduled."
"I take my calcium together with my iron."
"I'll eat protein first at each meal."

questions.stem: IV acetylcysteine is prescribed: 150 mg/kg over 1 hour, then 50 mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours. The client weighs 60 kg. How many milligrams are in the first (loading) dose? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 150 mg/kg x 60 kg = 9,000 mg over 1 hour. The total 21-hour course is 300 mg/kg, or 18,000 mg.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Twenty minutes into the loading dose, the client develops flushing, itching and wheezing. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give the prescribed antihistamine and bronchodilator
Restart at a slower rate once symptoms resolve, as prescribed
Leave the client alone to rest during the reaction

rationale.correct: Acetylcysteine reactions are treated and the infusion restarted more slowly; it is rarely abandoned.

perOption.a: A reaction to acetylcysteine, most common in the loading dose.
perOption.e: The benefit outweighs the reaction risk.

caseStudies.title: Leak after gastric bypass, then dumping syndrome

exhibits.title: Bariatric unit, postoperative day 1
exhibits.body: A 41-year-old client (BMI 48) had a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass yesterday. This morning the client says, "Something is wrong," and reports new left shoulder pain and pain in the upper abdomen. The client is breathing fast. Sips of water started at 0600.

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 0300
exhibits.body: A 19-year-old client says they swallowed "about 40" acetaminophen 500 mg tablets at about 2300 last night after a breakup. The client has mild nausea and otherwise feels fine. Weight 60 kg. The client says, "It doesn't matter what happens to me."

exhibits.title: Medical unit
exhibits.body: A 48-year-old client with alcohol use disorder has eaten almost nothing for 3 weeks. BMI 16. A central catheter was placed and parenteral nutrition was started yesterday at the full goal rate. Today the client is weak, short of breath and confused, with new ankle swelling.

exhibits.title: Endoscopy recovery, 1100
exhibits.body: A 66-year-old client had an upper endoscopy with balloon dilation of an esophageal stricture at 0930 under sedation. At 1100 the client reports severe pain behind the breastbone that goes to the back, and pain on swallowing. There is a crackling feeling under the skin of the neck when pressed.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
